description: Engineering strategy document reporting technical strategy or roadmap choices to management: the Rumelt kernel (diagnosis / guiding policy / coherent actions), a SCQA opening, and a policy-first reading order.

rules.instruction: Every guiding policy passes Applicable / Enforced / Creates Leverage (the Primer quality gate).
A policy must state what it gives up ("choosing A means not doing B"); a policy without a tradeoff is fluff.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; Rumelt, Good Strategy Bad Strategy, Ch. 5 (§2.2)

rules.instruction: Fluff, failure to face the challenge, goals-as-strategy, bad objectives — checked item by item at review.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; Rumelt, Good Strategy Bad Strategy, Ch. 3-4 (§2.2)

rules.instruction: Policies are stated as ratios / thresholds / mechanisms ("new services default to Rust unless X", "20% platform time each quarter"), not direction adjectives.
Assume a 1-2 page budget (vision-class documents cap at 2 pages), details behind links; assume the reader vanishes at page three.
The diagnosis retains data and reasoning (roadmap, competitive pressure, financial constraints, issues collected in 1:1s) for future readers to trace.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; Staff Engineer and Crafting Engineering Strategy, Ch. 11 (§2.2)

rules.instruction: Date, approval status, canonical-source link, and where to ask questions (a named channel or person).
Before release, an uninvolved reader flags unclear areas (carried by the workflow's review stage; noted in the SKILL.md routing text).

Close by turning each policy back on the reader as a yes/no audit question, and commit to a named revisit point (a date, an event, or an observable threshold) at which the strategy's effect will be reviewed; a strategy that ends on a restatement of its own goals has no way to be judged later.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; 2016 Letter to Shareholders (four closing audit questions), Engineering Executives' Primer, Ch. 3 (review impact after two months) (§2.2)

rules.instruction: Give each guiding policy a short name that survives being quoted out of context ("High-Velocity Decision Making", "Resist Proxies"); the name is the unit the organization repeats back, so an unnamed policy decays into a section number.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; 2016 Letter to Shareholders (four named defenses as section headings) (§2.2)

rules.instruction: State plainly what you do not know and how confident you are ("I don't know the whole answer, but I may know bits of it"); this is not fluff — fluff is empty confidence, while a stated limit tells the reader how much weight the reasoning carries.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; 2016 Letter to Shareholders (explicit epistemic downgrade), Rumelt, Ch. 3 (fluff is its own anti-pattern) (§2.2)

rules.instruction: Support the diagnosis with named incidents and first-hand observations, not only survey averages: a single traced anecdote carries the mechanism and the stakes, where a percentage alone is hard to interpret and can mislead.
rules.rationale: design §5.4; 2016 Letter to Shareholders (many anecdotes rather than only survey averages) (§2.2)

structure.audienceVariantNote: Approval audience: policy first. Org rollout: policy + operations first. Diagnosis and explore go last but must not be deleted. / 审批场景 policy 前置；组织落地场景 policy+operations 前置；diagnosis/explore 殿后但不可删。
